title: Simulating Green Beard Altruism
beats: If evolution rewards the fittest, why are creatures ever nice to each other?
Blobs forage daily; trees feed two; predators eat unlucky blobs; survivors reproduce. Genes will code behaviour rules.
Run the no-altruism world bigger and longer to show a stable baseline before adding anything.
Add the altruism choice: coward (run) vs altruist (warn, 50% risk). One gene, two alleles, yellow vs blue.
Real behaviour is many genes plus environment; this model is only good enough for fundamentals.
Allele-frequency stacked graph introduced, explained as always summing to 100%, after the sim has been watched.
Altruism goes extinct; try easy mode (10% death), goes extinct again.
Why one run is not enough; 30 runs; explicit prediction prompt with the reason predicting helps learning.
Thin lines are runs, thick line is average.
Exact tally of blobs saved vs lost shows altruism nets positive but population is capped, so only relative competition matters.
How could altruists help themselves more than rivals? Need a visible tag: the green beard.
Green beard altruism wins decisively; test 50% and 90% death over 30 runs each, predict first.
Start at 10% frequency: 11 of 30 runs fixate, 19 go extinct; luck dominates small numbers.
Advantage is frequency dependent: more beards means more helping.
Recall the caveat: one allele does two jobs. Split into beard gene and altruism gene.
Four types named and coloured: cowards, suckers, impostors, true beards; blobs see beards, not colours.
Prediction, then averages only (individual lines are a Jackson Pollock); suckers die first, true beards get exploited by impostors.
Green beard breaks with a little complexity, rare in nature; feels discouraging.
Next: kin selection and Hamilton's rule.

metrics.misconception: partial: assumes altruism should spread because it saves blobs; net saved copies does not matter, relative competition does (5:34)
metrics.brute_force: yes 0:49: run the world with no altruism, then run altruism repeatedly and watch extinction before any theory
metrics.examples: 4 sims escalating: altruism 50%, altruism 10%, 30-run batches, green beard 50/90%, 10% start, then 4-type split
metrics.ending: Honest downer plus teaser for kin selection; sponsor read

principles.1: confirmed: opens on 'why be nice' and a foraging blob day before any genetics (0:01-0:49)
principles.2: confirmed: only one new graph type at a time; colours and names added one by one; beard chosen as vivid proxy (6:22)
principles.3: partly: the allele graph and thin/thick lines are re-used all video so reading them becomes habit (4:44, 11:04)
principles.4: partly: beard is a stand-in for any detectable tag, no real analogy leaving; rigor comes through simulation tallies (5:00)
principles.5: confirmed: blobs literally go to trees, predators eat them, warn or flee on screen (1:38)
principles.6: confirmed: baseline no-altruism run, then single runs, then 30-run batches (0:49, 4:12)
principles.7: confirmed: repeated prediction pauses at 4:29, 6:38, 7:29, 8:01, 10:43 then reveal
principles.8: partly: idea rate slows on prediction pauses and long silent sim runs (several 30-40 s of music) rather than speech rate
principles.9: confirmed: same 30-run frame at different death chances and start frequencies (7:29, 8:01)
principles.10: confirmed: one gene two alleles, then green beard, then split into 2 genes and 4 types (9:39)
principles.11: confirmed: failure of plain altruism creates need for tag, tag creates need for split-gene test
principles.12: partly: links to papers and real-world rarity in description (11:53)
principles.13: partly: plain language ('easy mode', 'Jackson Pollock') plus exact counts like 225,817 saved (5:17)

new_moves.name: audit-the-win
new_moves.what: Instead of declaring the winner, count exactly who was saved and show why the headline number is the wrong metric
new_moves.evidence: 5:00-5:51 net saved copies positive yet extinction; competition is what matters

new_moves.name: sanity-test-the-winner
new_moves.what: After success, stress it with lower starting frequency, harsher cost, then splitting its bundled job into parts

new_moves.name: explain-why-predict
new_moves.what: Name the cognitive reason for making predictions (hindsight bias) once, then prompt repeatedly

theory: The video teaches by running a model, letting it fail, and using each failure to motivate the next small design change, always with a predict-then-reveal pause. The learner reconstructs why green beards work and then why they break, rather than being told. A caveat planted early (2:25) is cashed in later (9:22), turning honesty into the next step.
velocity: Scene builder: support batch runs (N runs, thin lines plus average) as a first-class scene primitive and pause before reveal.
Orchestrator: insert a predict-first beat before every reveal; log learner's prediction for the learner model.
Voice: plant an honest caveat early and callback to it when complexity is added.
Evals: check that each added mechanic comes from the previous failure.
quote: A successful allele for altruism would need to help itself more than competitor
